mechanism_narrative: The four-week decline in WORKPLACES mobility reflects a sustained reduction in commuting and associated incidental shopping trips, which mechanically depresses RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks as fewer people pass near retail precincts during work hours.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -21.7 to -50.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing a monotonic multi-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls past a -45 point threshold, this signals binding stage-4-style movement restrictions (e.g. curfew, 5km radius limits) are in force, which will further suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as non-essential retail trips become legally constrained.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -45 percent from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks even though TRANSIT remains below -45 for the same period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp week-on-week drops in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compound each other: reduced workplace attendance removes the transit-linked retail stop-ins, while reduced transit use removes the workplace-linked retail stop-ins, producing a larger combined suppression of RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, lasting four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT dropped sharply in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no larger (in magnitude) than what a single-series linear model using only WORKPLACES or only TRANSIT would predict.

mechanism_narrative: The rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility to 5.0 combined with the steep one-week drop in WORKPLACES to -50.1 indicates compliance with newly enforced stage-4 stay-at-home orders; under this enforcement regime, RETAIL_REC will fall further within one week as households minimize non-essential outings.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 4.5 while WORKPLACES falls below -45 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.7 to 5.0 while WORKPLACES fell to -50.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall (or rises) in the week immediately following a joint RESIDENTIAL>4.5 and WORKPLACES<-45 reading.

mechanism_narrative: The large week-on-week swing in PARKS (37.1 to 58.0) reflects winter weather variability rather than policy change; when PARKS spikes sharply upward after a dip, it indicates a transient good-weather window that temporarily substitutes for enclosed retail visits, producing a short-lived additional dip in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks before reverting.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 37.1 to 58.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no additional decline (relative to its prior trend) in the two weeks following a PARKS spike greater than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: The parallel decline of GROCERY_PHARM alongside RETAIL_REC indicates households are consolidating all shopping, including retail-adjacent errands, into fewer essential grocery/pharmacy trips; this substitution pattern will persist and continue to pull RETAIL_REC downward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -17.4 to -27.1 over four weeks, tracking RETAIL_REC's decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM decouple, with RETAIL_REC rising while GROCERY_PHARM continues to fall over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES crosses below -50 percent from baseline, it signals that stage-4 business-closure directives have taken full effect; under this threshold, RETAIL_REC will continue to decline for at least two more weeks as closures of non-essential retail and limited trading hours persist.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -50 percent from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or improves within two weeks of WORKPLACES first crossing below -50.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL and fall in GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week suggests a stockpiling/panic-buying episode followed by withdrawal into the home; this combined signal predicts a further one-week drop in RETAIL_REC as households front-load essential purchases and then minimize all further outings, including retail.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.0 while GROCERY_PHARM fell to -27.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a joint occurrence of RESIDENTIAL increase and GROCERY_PHARM decrease beyond their respective four-week trend rates.
